snippets.title: Three replicas, maintained by a controller
snippets.description: Deleting one Pod does not change replicas: 3. The Deployment’s ReplicaSet creates a new Pod to restore that count.

snippets.title: Internal Service
snippets.description: With type omitted, the Service defaults to ClusterIP. It selects app=web Pods in its own namespace.

snippets.title: Inspect a crash loop
snippets.description: Replace the example Pod and namespace. Events and the previous container log help reveal the cause; CrashLoopBackOff describes retry backoff, not the cause itself.

snippets.title: Read the terminated container’s log
snippets.description: --previous targets the prior terminated instance of container web, if its log is still available.

snippets.title: Readiness controls traffic
snippets.description: Three consecutive failed readiness checks mark this container unready. Readiness failure alone does not restart it.

snippets.title: Scheduling uses requests
snippets.description: This Pod needs two CPUs of schedulable requested capacity on one eligible node; capacity spread across nodes cannot satisfy one Pod.

snippets.title: Stable identities and one PVC per replica
snippets.description: The StatefulSet creates db-0 and db-1, each with its own data PVC. The headless Service supplies network identity; provisioning requires suitable storage.

snippets.title: Trace a Service selector
snippets.description: Compare the actual Service selector to Pod labels first, then inspect EndpointSlices and readiness. Names and namespace are examples.

snippets.title: A ClusterRole bound in one namespace
snippets.description: The ClusterRole is reusable, but this RoleBinding grants its namespaced Pod permissions only in demo. The demo namespace and app ServiceAccount must exist.

snippets.title: Encoding is not encryption
snippets.description: ZGVtbw== is only base64 for the dummy string demo. Anyone who can read the Secret can decode it; encryption at rest and access controls are separate concerns.

snippets.title: Give startup time before other probes
snippets.description: Startup gets about 300 seconds before its failure threshold. Liveness and readiness do not start until the startup probe succeeds.

snippets.title: Liveness can restart a container
snippets.description: Once liveness checking is active, three consecutive failures trigger container restart behavior. A readiness probe would affect traffic instead.

snippets.title: Millicpu units
snippets.description: 250m / 1000m = 0.25 CPU requested. The separate CPU limit here is 0.5 CPU.

snippets.title: Investigate OOM termination
snippets.description: Inspect the last termination reason and configured memory limits. top needs a metrics pipeline and shows current usage, which can miss the earlier peak.

snippets.title: Compare allocation with actual usage
snippets.description: Node description shows allocated resource requests. top measures observed usage; a low measurement does not free capacity already committed by requests.

snippets.title: Roll out without reducing availability
snippets.description: Four desired replicas plus one surge permits five non-terminating Pods during rollout while keeping four available. Terminating Pods can temporarily raise the total observed count.

snippets.title: Investigate image-pull failures
snippets.description: Events often name a missing tag or denied registry access. Check the referenced credentials and connectivity without printing Secret values.

snippets.title: Regular init containers run first
snippets.description: prepare must exit successfully before web starts. If it exits nonzero, Kubernetes retries it and the application stays blocked.

snippets.title: One agent on each eligible node
snippets.description: A DaemonSet maintains a Pod per eligible node. This toy heartbeat agent demonstrates placement; it does not collect real host logs.

snippets.title: Run a task to completion
snippets.description: The Job tracks successful completion and limits failed retries with backoffLimit. It is not intended to keep a web process running forever.

snippets.title: Avoid overlap within one CronJob
snippets.description: If a previous Job from this CronJob is still running at the next five-minute schedule, Forbid skips the overlapping start.

snippets.title: Service port versus target port
snippets.description: Clients use Service port 80; selected Pods receive traffic on 8080. The application must actually listen on that destination port.

snippets.title: Check ready endpoints
snippets.description: Compare selectors, readiness conditions, and EndpointSlice ready flags. publishNotReadyAddresses is an explicit Service exception to normal readiness filtering.

snippets.title: Cross-namespace DNS
snippets.description: api is the Service, backend is its namespace, and cluster.local is the assumed cluster domain. Replace the domain if your cluster uses another suffix.

snippets.title: Ingress needs a controller
snippets.description: A controller for the nginx class must already be installed, and Service web must exist. This object alone does not deploy a controller or provision DNS.

snippets.title: NetworkPolicy permissions add together
snippets.description: With NetworkPolicy enforcement enabled, both policies select app=web. Together they allow inbound TCP on 80 and 443 from all sources; one does not override the other.

snippets.title: Allow DNS through restricted egress
snippets.description: This selects DNS Pods in kube-system with the assumed kube-dns label, allowing TCP and UDP 53. Verify your DNS labels and CNI behavior; NodeLocal DNS may need a different destination rule.

snippets.title: ConfigMap environment snapshot
snippets.description: MODE is populated when the container starts. Updating the ConfigMap does not change the environment in this running process; replace or restart the container.

snippets.title: subPath does not receive ConfigMap updates
snippets.description: Mounting the individual key with subPath prevents automatic updates to that mount. A normal ConfigMap volume has different projection behavior.

snippets.title: Investigate a Pending claim
snippets.description: PVC events identify missing storage classes, provisioning failures, or incompatible volume requirements. Some StorageClasses intentionally wait for a consumer before binding.

snippets.title: ReadWriteOnce is node-scoped
snippets.description: RWO means read-write on one node. Several Pods on that same node can share it if the driver and workload permit; it is not a single-Pod guarantee. A suitable default StorageClass or matching PV is needed.

snippets.title: Retain preserves storage for manual handling
snippets.description: After claim deletion, Retain leaves reclamation to an administrator. hostPath is only a single-node teaching example, not a portable production storage design.

snippets.title: Toleration removes one scheduling barrier
snippets.description: This tolerates dedicated=batch:NoSchedule. It neither forces placement on such nodes nor overrides other resource and affinity constraints.

snippets.title: Require a node label
snippets.description: Only nodes labeled disktype=ssd match. If none also satisfy the remaining constraints, this Pod stays Pending.

snippets.title: Separate replicas across nodes
snippets.description: Required anti-affinity prevents matching replicas in the same namespace from sharing a hostname domain. Fewer than three eligible nodes can leave replicas unscheduled.

snippets.title: Cordon versus drain
snippets.description: Cordon blocks ordinary new scheduling; drain also attempts eviction. Drain may stop for PDBs, unmanaged Pods, or local data; inspect blockers rather than forcing past them.

snippets.title: Keep two replicas available
snippets.description: With three healthy matching replicas, one voluntary eviction is normally allowed. This budget does not guarantee protection against node failure or every direct deletion.

snippets.title: get and list are different verbs
snippets.description: When bound, this grants reading a named Pod, not listing the collection. kubectl get pods performs a list request; adding list would grant that operation.

snippets.title: Choose the workload identity
snippets.description: Assuming namespace demo exists, this Pod uses demo/app. A mounted token authenticates as that ServiceAccount; separate RBAC grants determine what it can do.

snippets.title: Enforce a numeric non-root user
snippets.description: runAsNonRoot enforces the non-root condition, and runAsUser selects UID 1000. The image and writable paths must support that UID.

snippets.title: A writable exception to a read-only root
snippets.description: The image root filesystem is read-only, but /tmp is a separate writable emptyDir. That data is temporary and tied to the Pod’s lifetime.

snippets.title: Allow time for graceful shutdown
snippets.description: The kubelet gives the container a termination window. If processes remain after the grace period, they can be forcibly killed; the application still needs proper shutdown handling.

snippets.title: HPA utilization uses CPU requests
snippets.description: For a container using 200m with a 500m request, utilization is 40%. This target uses average request-relative utilization; it requires the target workload, CPU requests, and metrics support.

snippets.title: An aggregate namespace resource budget
snippets.description: The quota bounds totals in demo, not each individual container. New admissions exceeding a hard limit are rejected; creating the quota does not resize existing containers.

snippets.title: Default requests and limits at admission
snippets.description: A newly admitted container omitting memory settings gets a 128Mi request and 256Mi limit. Minimum and maximum constraints bound its allowed memory settings. Running containers are unchanged; namespace demo must exist.

snippets.title: Add diagnostic tools without rebuilding
snippets.description: An ephemeral container supplies tools alongside the application. Admission policy, permissions, and container-runtime support determine which debugging features are available.

snippets.title: Choose a container for exec
snippets.description: -c api chooses the container; everything after -- is the command inside it. This example assumes cat is installed in that image.

snippets.title: Selectors combine equality requirements
snippets.description: The comma means AND: a selected Pod must have both app=web and tier=frontend in demo.

snippets.title: Inspect history before rollback
snippets.description: Rollback uses retained Deployment Pod-template history. It does not restore a database or undo separately changed ConfigMaps.

snippets.title: Keep unrelated selectors distinct
snippets.description: Use distinct identifying labels for unrelated controllers and keep each template consistent with its selector. Do not create another unrelated controller selecting the same label set.

snippets.title: Initialize before validating
snippets.description: init prepares providers, modules, and the selected backend. validate then checks structure; neither command is an apply. Run only in the intended configuration directory.

snippets.title: Check formatting without edits
snippets.description: A nonzero exit status reports formatting differences. This checks formatting, not credentials or remote infrastructure.

snippets.title: Validate without contacting a backend
snippets.description: This prepares dependencies without initializing a remote backend. validate checks syntax and internal consistency, not a live infrastructure plan.

snippets.title: Preview managed-resource changes
snippets.description: Plan proposes operations and can read remote objects through providers. It does not carry out the proposed managed-resource changes.

snippets.title: Review and apply the same saved plan
snippets.description: Review the saved plan before apply. Treat the plan file as sensitive because it can include state and input values.

snippets.title: Inspect state bindings
snippets.description: State addresses map configuration instances to tracked objects. state show can expose sensitive attributes; use these commands only with the intended state and access.

snippets.title: Sensitive does not mean absent from state
snippets.description: The variable is marked sensitive, but using it as a normal persisted resource input can still put it in state. The dummy value demonstrates display marking, not secure secret storage.

snippets.title: Redact a normal output display
snippets.description: Ordinary output display is redacted. Explicit raw or JSON output can reveal it, and sensitive marking does not by itself remove it from state.

snippets.title: Remote state locking configuration
snippets.description: This S3 backend opts into a lockfile. The bucket must already exist and access policies must permit state and lock operations; backend support and permissions control actual locking.

snippets.title: Wait for a lock rather than bypass it
snippets.description: This allows time to acquire the existing state lock. Coordinate with the teammate holding it rather than using -lock=false.

snippets.title: Select a separate workspace state
snippets.description: Select an existing dev workspace to use its state. CLI workspaces share the configuration and are not a security-isolation boundary.

snippets.title: Provider constraints choose acceptable versions
snippets.description: ~> 6.21.0 permits versions from 6.21.0 up to, but not including, 6.22.0. The dependency lock file records the exact selected version.

snippets.title: Share the dependency lock file
snippets.description: Commit the root configuration’s lock file along with its provider constraints. The file records providers, not infrastructure state or remote module version locks.

snippets.title: Constrain the Terraform CLI
snippets.description: The comma combines constraints: a Terraform CLI at least 1.5.0 and below 2.0.0 is required. This says nothing about provider versions.

snippets.title: Call a local module
snippets.description: ./modules/network is a directory relative to this calling module. The companion teaching fixture exports a dummy subnet_id; it does not create a cloud subnet.

snippets.title: Read a child module’s output
snippets.description: The caller consumes the declared subnet_id output through module.network.subnet_id. It does not reach directly into the child’s internal resources.

snippets.title: Name a reusable expression
snippets.description: local.app_name evaluates to quiz-dev with the default input. A local is a named expression, not a mutable variable.

snippets.title: Reject non-positive replica counts
snippets.description: Zero and negative numbers fail this condition. It only enforces positivity; it does not by itself require an integer.

snippets.title: count creates zero-based instances
snippets.description: The addresses are terraform_data.worker[0], [1], and [2]. The built-in terraform_data resource needs no external provider plugin.

snippets.title: A set removes duplicate instance keys
snippets.description: The set has just api and worker, so Terraform creates two instances keyed by those strings. Set order is not an instance identity.

snippets.title: Map keys and values
snippets.description: For the prod instance, each.key is prod and each.value is 3. The numeric value is separate from the stable string instance key.

snippets.title: Keep instance keys known during planning
snippets.description: api is a known configuration key even though the new source ID is unknown until apply. Putting that unknown ID in the key set instead would prevent Terraform from planning instance identities.

snippets.title: Choose one expansion mechanism
snippets.description: This block uses for_each only. count and for_each are mutually exclusive on the same resource block.

snippets.title: A reference creates an implicit dependency
snippets.description: The subnet_id reference makes web depend on app. The VPC and AMI IDs are dummy examples and must be replaced with compatible objects before any real plan or apply.

snippets.title: Declare a hidden behavioral dependency
snippets.description: This toy marker illustrates explicit ordering when no argument reference expresses the dependency. In real infrastructure, use depends_on only for a real hidden dependency, not as a substitute for ordinary references.

snippets.title: Create a replacement first
snippets.description: When triggers_replace changes on an existing instance, replacement is requested with create-before-destroy ordering. Real provider resources may still hit naming, capacity, or coexistence constraints.

snippets.title: A configuration-based destruction guard
snippets.description: While this lifecycle rule is present, a plan that destroys this instance is rejected. Removing the whole resource block removes this configuration-based protection too.

snippets.title: Ignore an attribute during updates
snippets.description: input is still used at creation. Afterward, differences in that attribute are ignored for update planning; this can also conceal drift.

snippets.title: Record a resource-address rename
snippets.description: If state already tracks terraform_data.web, the moved block explains its new address. It avoids treating a pure rename as an unrelated delete and create.

snippets.title: Import an existing object into state
snippets.description: The import command records a binding; it does not write all the desired resource configuration for you. Replace the example bucket name and review the full plan afterward.

snippets.title: Declare an import in configuration
snippets.description: This declares the existing bucket to bind to aws_s3_bucket.logs during apply. The name is an example; credentials and a real matching bucket are required for an actual import.

snippets.title: Remove a binding, leave the remote object
snippets.description: state rm forgets the binding. If the resource block remains, the next normal plan can propose creating a replacement object, so review configuration and state together.

snippets.title: Review observed drift separately
snippets.description: The saved refresh-only plan reconciles state with observed changes rather than proposing ordinary configuration-driven resource updates. Applying still changes state and outputs.

snippets.title: Targeted recovery followed by a full plan
snippets.description: -target narrows the graph and can leave other changes outside the result. The subsequent full plan exposes work omitted by the targeted plan.

snippets.title: Request replacement in a plan
snippets.description: The example address is explicitly marked for replacement in the proposal. This does not apply the replacement; review its dependency and disruption impact first.

snippets.title: Read an existing object with a data source
snippets.description: The data block reads an AMI matching these filters in the configured account and region; it does not create the image. A real plan fails if no suitable owned image matches.

snippets.title: Generate repeated nested blocks
snippets.description: dynamic emits two ingress blocks, one for each port. The example VPC ID is a placeholder; dynamic cannot generate arbitrary top-level resource or lifecycle blocks.

snippets.title: Transform a list with a for expression
snippets.description: The result is ["API", "WORKER"]. This transforms values; it does not create resource instances.

snippets.title: Select the false branch
snippets.description: With enabled=false, the result is 0. Both branches are numbers, so their types are compatible.

snippets.title: Use a fallback for an absent map key
snippets.description: test is absent, so lookup returns the fallback 1. It does not mutate the map or add a test key.

snippets.title: Handle a missing decoded attribute
snippets.description: The decoded object has no retries attribute, so try returns 3. try handles dynamic evaluation errors, not malformed HCL or undeclared identifiers.

snippets.title: null represents absence
snippets.description: This accepts an absent description and reports not supplied. In many provider arguments, null acts as omission; whether that is allowed and which default applies depend on the argument schema.

snippets.title: Flatten directly nested sequences
snippets.description: The result is ["a", "b", "c"]. flatten removes directly nested list layers, not every collection hidden inside an object or map.

snippets.title: Later merge arguments win
snippets.description: The result keeps env=dev and sets team=platform because the later map wins for duplicate keys. This is a shallow merge.

snippets.title: Select a numbered subnet
snippets.description: Adding eight prefix bits produces /24 subnets. Zero-based netnum 2 picks 10.0.2.0/24, the third subnet.

snippets.title: Iterate a map of resource instances
snippets.description: for_each produces a map. The for expression iterates its values to collect IDs; the AMI is a dummy and the resulting IDs are unknown until real creation.

snippets.title: Wire a provider alias into a child
snippets.description: The child module’s aws slot receives the caller’s west configuration. The companion child fixture declares the provider requirement; this is separate from ordinary module input variables.

snippets.title: Keep dependencies one-way
snippets.description: This corrected graph has app depend on network. Making network also depend on app would form a cycle; moving blocks between files cannot solve it.

snippets.title: Concurrency does not replace the graph
snippets.description: Terraform still respects dependencies with one worker. Resources are not executed in file order simply because concurrency is limited.

snippets.title: Use partial backend configuration
snippets.description: Backend settings are supplied during initialization, before ordinary variable evaluation. Replace the bucket name; avoid putting credentials in backend arguments or committed files.

snippets.title: CPU units — lab reference
snippets.description: This corrected teaching manifest requests 100m, or 0.1 CPU. The lab’s original "1000" requests 1,000 CPUs and cannot fit a normal lab node; namespace virtmicro-lab must exist.

snippets.title: Admission versus scheduling — lab reference
snippets.description: A missing Pod plus the original admission error points to object creation, not a container runtime failure. Read the exact rejected resource and quota before changing the request.

snippets.title: Scheduling evidence — lab reference
snippets.description: Look for an empty NODE column, PodScheduled=False, and the event reason. Other scheduling constraints can appear in the same event.

snippets.title: Per-node capacity — lab reference
snippets.description: Allocatable is only the starting budget. Compare each candidate node’s allocated requests and remaining capacity; do not sum spare CPU across nodes for one Pod.

snippets.title: Standalone Pod ownership — lab reference
snippets.description: Check ownership before assuming Kubernetes will recreate a deleted Pod. The lab explicitly reapplies this standalone object.

snippets.title: Verify a scheduling repair — lab reference
snippets.description: Ready plus an assigned node verifies more than admission success. A timeout is a prompt to inspect the current events and conditions, not proof that CPU remains the cause.

snippets.title: Constrain the experiment — lab reference
snippets.description: Replace colima with the selected node’s actual hostname label. This hard selector excludes other hostnames; it does not tolerate any taint.

snippets.title: Match the taint precisely — lab reference
snippets.description: This toleration matches the lab taint. Add the lab’s hostname selector as well if placement must remain on the selected node.

snippets.title: NoSchedule and existing Pods — lab reference
snippets.description: Existing Pods are not evicted merely by adding NoSchedule. The commands change a node and are reference examples, not part of automated QA.

snippets.title: NoExecute differs — lab reference
snippets.description: This tolerates the specified NoExecute taint for 60 seconds after it is added, after which eviction can occur if the taint remains. It is distinct from the lab’s NoSchedule toleration.

snippets.title: Deployment Pod templates — lab reference
snippets.description: The toleration is in the Pod template, so the Deployment carries it into replacement Pods. It still does not force placement on a particular node.

snippets.title: Clean up node-level changes — lab reference
snippets.description: Remove only the lab-owned taint. A missing-taint response is expected if it was already removed; do not remove unrelated node protections.

snippets.title: Establish a healthy baseline — lab reference
snippets.description: Verify the starting Deployment before deliberately changing its image. These checks observe the rollout and do not introduce the failure.

snippets.title: Rolling-update availability — lab reference
snippets.description: This preserves two available replicas during a normal controlled rollout and permits one surge Pod. It cannot protect against every involuntary failure or guarantee capacity for the surge.

snippets.title: Read the registry error — lab reference
snippets.description: Read the image name and exact pull error in Events. Do not assume a deliberately bad tag caused the failure if the registry instead reports authentication or connectivity trouble.

snippets.title: Logs before container creation — lab reference
snippets.description: Inspect containerStatuses and Events for a waiting reason such as ImagePullBackOff. An application that never started has no current application output to inspect.

snippets.title: Progress deadline — lab reference
snippets.description: Look at the Progressing condition and its reason, alongside ReplicaSet and Pod status. A progress deadline is not an automatic rollback policy.

snippets.title: Client timeout versus controller deadline — lab reference
snippets.description: A timed-out waiting command does not stop the controller. Inspect its actual conditions and configured deadline before deciding what failed.

snippets.title: Surge capacity — lab reference
snippets.description: Distinguish an empty NODE and FailedScheduling from a scheduled Pod waiting for an image. Both can stall a rollout, but at different stages.

snippets.title: Available does not mean updated — lab reference
snippets.description: Healthy old replicas can maintain availability while updatedReplicas or progress signals reveal that the new version is not ready.

snippets.title: Service traffic during rollout — lab reference
snippets.description: Correlate ready EndpointSlice addresses with Pod IPs and images to identify which replicas can serve. A successful response alone does not verify the newest revision.

snippets.title: Verify a rollout repair — lab reference
snippets.description: Verify the intended image and updated replicas rather than only checking that some replicas are available. Endpoint readiness supplies separate traffic-path evidence.

snippets.title: Container names in an image update — lab reference
snippets.description: Match web to the actual template container name before changing its image. stable-alpine is convenient for the disposable exercise; controlled releases should use immutable image references.

snippets.title: Control-plane taints in a lab — lab reference
snippets.description: Replace colima with your selected lab node. Check its existing taints first and record which lab-owned change, if any, you introduce.

snippets.title: ReplicaSet creation failures — interview reference
snippets.description: No Pod object means there may be no Pod scheduling event to read. Inspect the ReplicaSet that is trying to create the Pod, and preserve the exact rejection message.

snippets.title: Pending after assignment — interview reference
snippets.description: Read node assignment, conditions, container waiting reasons, and Events together. A single phase label does not establish the failure stage.

snippets.title: EBS Availability Zone constraints — interview reference
snippets.description: Confirm a topology-related scheduling event and compare the actual PV node-affinity terms with node labels. A volume name alone does not establish the diagnosis.

snippets.title: Trace Pod to disk topology — interview reference
snippets.description: Replace data and pv-example with names discovered in the preceding output. Compare actual affinity keys and values, including CSI-specific keys, to real node labels.

snippets.title: WaitForFirstConsumer limits — interview reference
snippets.description: This example requires an installed and authorized EBS CSI driver on AWS. The binding mode influences new claims; it does not migrate already-bound EBS volumes.

snippets.title: CPU limits and throttling — interview reference
snippets.description: The deliberate busy loop can demand more CPU, but its CPU limit is 500m. Investigate throttling and latency separately from OOM or application-exit failures; this reference is not executed by QA.

snippets.title: Requests without CPU limits — interview reference
snippets.description: This declared container has no CPU limit. Admission policies such as LimitRange may inject one, so inspect the admitted Pod before concluding that no limit applies at runtime.

snippets.title: Direct node assignment — interview reference
snippets.description: Label exactly the intended lab node with lab.example.com/worker=worker-a first. This selector leaves the scheduler responsible for evaluating requests and other placement constraints.

snippets.title: Unavailable required node — interview reference
snippets.description: Only nodes with the required label are candidates. This provides strict placement, not failover to an arbitrary worker; using a unique label deliberately narrows availability.

snippets.title: Strict SSD node placement — interview reference
snippets.description: This hard node-affinity rule requires disktype=ssd at scheduling time. Labels must accurately describe the node; the rule does not provision application storage.

snippets.title: SSD node labels versus persistent storage — interview reference
snippets.description: On AWS with a working EBS CSI driver, this claim requests gp3-backed storage. A consuming Pod must reference app-data in a volume and mount it; node selection is a separate decision.

snippets.title: Production pool security — interview reference
snippets.description: Review identities, namespace permissions, admission enforcement, and network/resource controls together. These checks are evidence to gather, not proof that the whole isolation policy is correct.

snippets.title: Release controls versus runtime isolation — interview reference
snippets.description: Inspect runtime controls independently of repository settings. Separate clusters/accounts may be chosen for stronger boundaries, but a protected branch alone creates neither design.

snippets.title: Artifact promotion and deployment identity — interview reference
snippets.description: The pipeline should promote the reviewed image digest and obtain the appropriate scoped identity for each environment. These read-only checks do not configure OIDC or implement CI approval rules.

snippets.title: Intentional GPU-pool taint — interview reference
snippets.description: The unscheduled Pod has no assigned node. Inspect the candidate GPU node and other pools, then choose placement that respects the reservation policy.

snippets.title: Health-related taints — interview reference
snippets.description: Replace worker-1 with a candidate named by your investigation. Events summarize scheduler reasons and can expire, so use current conditions and taints as well.

snippets.title: Monitoring pool placement — interview reference
snippets.description: Assumes intended nodes carry workload-pool=monitoring and the same key/value NoSchedule taint. This demo sleeps; it illustrates placement rather than installing a monitoring stack.

snippets.title: Migrate existing non-monitoring workloads — interview reference
snippets.description: Drain cordons the node and can stop on constraints. Do not bypass blockers blindly; these reference commands change node availability and are syntax-checked rather than executed by QA.

snippets.title: Drain exceptions — interview reference
snippets.description: Inspect ownerReferences and the kubernetes.io/config.mirror annotation to distinguish DaemonSet and static-Pod cases. Other blockers can prevent a drain from completing.

snippets.title: Hostname versus zone topology — interview reference
snippets.description: This constrains spread of matching Pods across eligible hostname domains at scheduling time. It does not automatically relocate already-running replicas.

snippets.title: What maxSkew does not guarantee — interview reference
snippets.description: With exactly three eligible domains and no competing constraints, 2/1/1 is compatible with this bound. Eligibility, other matching Pods, and additional constraint settings affect real scheduling.

snippets.title: Hard versus preferred spread — interview reference
snippets.description: This prefers balancing matching Pods across hostname domains. Choose DoNotSchedule when the skew requirement must block otherwise eligible placement, accepting that Pods can remain Pending.

snippets.title: Existing replica redistribution — interview reference
snippets.description: A template edit already starts a Deployment rollout; an extra rollout restart is not inherently required. Verify new Pod placement, and inspect events if strict constraints prevent replacements from scheduling.

snippets.title: Combining zone and node distribution — interview reference
snippets.description: Requires accurate zone and hostname labels on candidate nodes. These rules bound skew over eligible domains; they do not guarantee a particular number of AZs exist or relocate existing zonal volumes.

snippets.title: Inventory — ansible-001
snippets.description: Inventory group headings assign the following hosts to that group until another heading begins.

snippets.title: Inventory — ansible-002
snippets.description: all includes every inventory host. ungrouped contains hosts that belong to no other group apart from all.

snippets.title: Host patterns — ansible-003
snippets.description: The & intersection operator limits the selection to hosts in both groups. Quoting prevents the shell from interpreting special characters.

snippets.title: Connectivity — ansible-004
snippets.description: The Ansible ping module is not network ICMP ping. It exercises the Ansible connection and remote module execution path.

snippets.title: Facts — ansible-005
snippets.description: setup gathers facts such as platform and interfaces. These facts can be referenced through ansible_facts during playbook execution.

snippets.title: Facts — ansible-006
snippets.description: Disabling automatic fact gathering can save time, but facts must come from another deliberate source before tasks rely on them. This reference gathers the minimum facts explicitly before reading them.

snippets.title: Privilege escalation — ansible-007
snippets.description: become requests privilege escalation. Its success depends on the remote account’s configured authorization and any required credentials.

snippets.title: Idempotency — ansible-008
snippets.description: Idempotency concerns repeated effects, not simply whether a command runs. Desired-state modules often inspect existing state before changing it.

snippets.title: Commands — ansible-009
snippets.description: command avoids shell interpretation, reducing quoting and injection risks. Use shell only when shell features are actually required.

snippets.title: Commands — ansible-010
snippets.description: command passes arguments without shell parsing. Use a suitable module or an explicitly justified shell task for pipelines. Here the pipe is passed as a literal argument; stdout is hello|wc-c, not a byte count.

snippets.title: Commands — ansible-011
snippets.description: creates is a guard checked before execution. The command or another task must actually create the marker when initialization succeeds. The illustrative /opt/app/init must exist and create the marker on success.

snippets.title: Handlers — ansible-012
snippets.description: Notifications are driven by changed status. A successful but unchanged task does not normally notify handlers. The app service is illustrative; syntax QA never restarts a service.

snippets.title: Handlers — ansible-013
snippets.description: Ansible deduplicates handler notifications within a handler execution phase. Handlers run in their defined order rather than notification order. The app service is illustrative; syntax QA never restarts a service.

snippets.title: Handlers — ansible-014
snippets.description: flush_handlers creates an earlier handler execution point. Later changed tasks may notify the same handlers again. The app service is illustrative; syntax QA never restarts a service.

snippets.title: Files — ansible-015
snippets.description: template renders Jinja on the controller before transferring content. copy is appropriate for content that does not require template rendering. The companion app.conf.j2 fixture contains port={{ http_port }}.

snippets.title: Permissions — ansible-016
snippets.description: Quoting permission modes avoids YAML numeric-interpretation surprises. The file module then applies the intended octal mode.

snippets.title: YAML and Jinja — ansible-017
snippets.description: YAML parses the document before Ansible renders expressions. Quoting avoids confusion with YAML mapping syntax.

snippets.title: Variables — ansible-018
snippets.description: Extra variables have very high variable precedence. Use them deliberately because they can override values from many other variable sources. Run with -e service_port=9090 to override the play value of 8080 as well.

snippets.title: Jinja filters — ansible-019
snippets.description: The default filter supplies a fallback for undefined values. Treating empty or false values as missing requires the filter’s optional boolean behavior.

snippets.title: Conditionals — ansible-020
snippets.description: Explicit conversion avoids treating a nonempty string as an intended boolean value. Modern conditionals should evaluate to booleans.

snippets.title: Conditionals — ansible-021
snippets.description: A list of when conditions is combined with logical AND. The condition is evaluated for each host executing the task.

snippets.title: Conditionals — ansible-022
snippets.description: An explicit or expression expresses alternative conditions. A YAML list of separate conditions would instead use AND.

snippets.title: Loops — ansible-023
snippets.description: A condition on a looping task is evaluated separately for each item.

snippets.title: Registered results — ansible-024
snippets.description: A registered looping task returns an aggregate result with a results list. Individual module result fields live inside those entries.

snippets.title: Changed status — ansible-025
snippets.description: changed_when controls change reporting. It does not alter execution, erase failures, or make a command idempotent by itself.

snippets.title: Failure conditions — ansible-026
snippets.description: A failed_when list combines expressions with AND. Use one expression with or if either condition should independently indicate failure.

snippets.title: Retries — ansible-027
snippets.description: until defines the success condition for retrying this task. retries and delay control the retry budget and waiting period.

snippets.title: Error handling — ansible-028
snippets.description: ignore_errors applies to ordinary task failure results, not every possible failure mode. Ansible has separate unreachable-host handling.

snippets.title: Blocks — ansible-029
snippets.description: rescue handles normal block task failures. Invalid task definitions and unreachable hosts are not ordinary rescuable failed results.

snippets.title: Blocks — ansible-030
snippets.description: always is used for actions such as cleanup after block execution. It does not overcome all fatal execution or connectivity problems.

snippets.title: Check mode — ansible-031
snippets.description: Check mode depends on module support and task behavior. Unsupported tasks may be skipped, and registered-result-dependent flows may not simulate fully.

snippets.title: Diff mode — ansible-032
snippets.description: Diff output can reveal file contents. Use appropriate output controls such as diff: false for sensitive tasks.

snippets.title: Vault — ansible-033
snippets.description: Vault protects stored content. Once decrypted for use, secrets still need careful handling in tasks, logs, and application configuration.

snippets.title: Secret handling — ansible-034
snippets.description: no_log suppresses normal task-result logging. Do not expose the same secret through a separate debug task or assume it solves every logging path.

snippets.title: Delegation — ansible-035
snippets.description: Delegation changes where the action runs. inventory_hostname still identifies the original host context, though other connection variables can come from the delegated host.

snippets.title: Execution control — ansible-036
snippets.description: run_once normally applies to the current host batch. If an operation truly must run once for the entire play, design its condition accordingly.

snippets.title: Rolling changes — ansible-037
snippets.description: serial bounds the batch of hosts progressing through the play. It is useful for rolling maintenance and controlled deployments.

snippets.title: Concurrency — ansible-038
snippets.description: throttle can constrain task concurrency below the broader worker or batch limits. It does not set a permanent host count.

snippets.title: Strategies — ansible-039
snippets.description: free lets hosts progress independently within applicable limits. Cross-host synchronization assumptions that fit linear execution may no longer hold.

snippets.title: Controller workers — ansible-040
snippets.description: forks affects parallel host work. serial, throttle, strategy, and target responsiveness can further limit effective concurrency.

snippets.title: Task reuse — ansible-041
snippets.description: Static imports are expanded earlier; dynamic includes are processed during execution. This affects conditionals, loops, and tag handling.

snippets.title: Tags — ansible-042
snippets.description: Dynamic includes need deliberate tag propagation, such as apply tags or tagging the included tasks. Tagging the include alone is not blanket inheritance.

snippets.title: Roles — ansible-043
snippets.description: Role defaults have low variable precedence and are designed for customization. Role vars have higher precedence and are harder for callers to override. The companion role defines service_port in defaults/main.yml and prints its effective value.

snippets.title: Handlers — ansible-044
snippets.description: listen topics decouple notifications from individual handler names. Multiple handlers can listen to the same topic. The app service is illustrative; syntax QA never restarts a service.

snippets.title: Collections — ansible-045
snippets.description: Fully qualified collection names clarify module resolution and reduce collisions with similarly named modules from other collections.

snippets.title: Host variables — ansible-046
snippets.description: hostvars exposes inventory-host variable contexts. Reading gathered facts from another host still requires those facts to be available.

snippets.title: Task environment — ansible-047
snippets.description: The environment keyword supplies environment variables for task execution. It does not permanently modify the controller or target account’s login configuration.

snippets.title: Asynchronous work — ansible-048
snippets.description: poll zero is fire-and-forget behavior for the launching task. Use the returned job information to inspect or wait for completion separately.

snippets.title: Asynchronous work — ansible-049
snippets.description: async_status uses the async job ID to retrieve status. A polling loop with until can wait for its finished result.

snippets.title: Validation — ansible-050
snippets.description: assert checks preconditions and produces a failure if its expression is false. Validation is distinct from actually provisioning the desired resource.
